cells.tense: You're holding two things that both matter and neither one is getting dropped.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've brought along that's done — not finished badly, just done — and let it close out loud.
cells.core:
You're steering, and the steering is calm. You already know what gets tended and what gets left, and you make that call the way a gardener decides which beds to water — deliberately, with a plan, without apology. Nothing here is being forced, and nothing is being clutched either. The two demands stay held, and you stay the one holding them.

The care runs on its own now. You put the work in and it stayed put, and what's growing is growing because of choices you made and kept making. The next thing this can feed is being told — by someone who watched you do it — that the tending was yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing what grows, and the choosing is steady.

cells.tense: You're managing a growing season that hasn't arrived, already exhausted from a harvest that isn't here.
cells.ask: Pick one thing on your list and let today's version of it be enough.
cells.core:
You're out ahead of it. The plan has plans — what comes after this, what happens when that works, what to do if it doesn't — and you've been holding the whole sequence at once, adjusting for outcomes that haven't happened. Tending turned into controlling somewhere back there, and the grip is the part that's tired.

Stewardship done well is looser than this. You put something in the ground, you water it, you leave it alone and it comes up the way it comes up — that's the version that doesn't run you down. Letting things be in process instead of already-decided is what opens the room for the satisfaction you're working toward.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping the outcome instead of tending the thing.

cells.tense: There's something you used to be tending and you set it down, and you've been standing near it without picking it back up.
cells.ask: Choose one small thing and tend it badly, today, just to prove the choosing still works.
cells.core:
The care didn't go anywhere. What's missing is the pick-up — the moment where you look at the thing and decide it's yours to look after, and then look after it. Somewhere the deciding stopped, and the stopping turned into the whole posture. Nothing is growing because nothing is being tended, and the nothing is starting to feel like the truth about you.

When this is working, you wake up knowing what you're pointed at and you point at it — that's the whole of it, no more than that. One thing, chosen and kept, and the day has its shape. The reach is still there. It just needs somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You know how to tend things. You stopped choosing what.
cells.place: the place where you choose what you're pointed at

cells.tense: You're already tending it — the daily upkeep is happening — but you'd call it just how things are.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person what you've been holding together, and let it count as something you did.
cells.core:
Look at what's actually being kept going around you. The routines, the repairs, the small maintenance nobody asked you to do — that's you, choosing, every day, and it's shaping everything in your orbit. You describe it as though it were happening on its own. It isn't happening on its own. It's your hands.

Stewardship that's working flexes like a grip that knows when to loosen — it holds what needs holding and releases what's finished, and it doesn't call that giving up. The claim just hasn't been made yet. Someone watching already sees it, and saying so out loud lets what you've been doing finally come back as yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one tending this, and the naming is still owed.
